features.text: Patient is 34 years old and female.
Patient has had lower back pain for about six days.
The back pain started when the patient was walking and her back seized up.
The back pain is located in the lower back and is not lateralized to one side.
The back pain is constant but worsens with certain movements such as bending or extending the back.
The patient has been taking ibuprofen and using heat for the back pain, but it remains stiff.
The patient has not experienced any numbness, tingling, or weakness in the legs.
The patient has not experienced any changes in bowel or bladder function.
The patient has not experienced any fever, chills, or unexplained weight loss.
The patient has not had any recent trauma or heavy lifting that could have contributed to the back spasm.
The patient has been lifting weights a few times a week, including deadlifts, about three times a week.
The patient has not had any prior episodes of back pain or muscle spasms.
The patient has not had any imaging studies of the spine in the past, except for an X-ray today that showed no fracture.
The patient has nasal congestion from allergies.
